title: Node boot sequencing lab notes
body:
Goal: capture a single-threaded lab reproduction and command journal for the intermittent node NotReady / kubelet crash loop we saw in EU-prod on 2026-02-25. Use as a checklist for next reprod and to seed troubleshooting runbook.

Quick summary of symptom seen in prod: node goes NotReady ~30-60s after provisioning; kubelet logs show repeated 'Failed to create PodSandbox' and then node registers NotReady with 'Kubelet has disk pressure' or occasionally 'eviction manager: imagefs available: 0%'. But nodes are new fresh instances (EBS empty).

Hypothesis snapshots (ranked):
- 1) Race in cloud-init + apt upgrade ordering -> container runtime install/config happens after kubelet starts and kubelet can't find CRI socket -> kubelet crash loops.
- 2) Wrong cgroup driver mismatch (containerd uses systemd but kubelet expecting cgroupfs) -> kubelet fails to create sandbox.
- 3) Missing sysctl for overlay/bridge -> CNI fails to attach, causing 'PodSandbox' failures and pod creation stalls.
- 4) Device mapper / ephemeral disk mount timing: kubelet thinks imagefs full due to mount not yet attached and path points to root.
- 5) kube-proxy / iptables rules corrupted by cloud-init scripts leading to node NotReady via failed readiness checks.

Commands I ran (chronological, with key outputs):

1) Basic system checks after repro (fresh VM repro)
- uname -a
  Linux node-b4 5.15.0-1029-aws #32-Ubuntu SMP Thu Jul 8 10:12:31 UTC 2025 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- cat /etc/os-release
  Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS

2) systemd / unit status
- systemctl status kubelet -l --no-pager
  "kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE"
  journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 showed repeated: "E0325 14:21:03.123456 kubelet.go:225] failed to create kubelet: failed to get runtime version: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 127.0.0.1:10250: connect: connection refused""

- systemctl status containerd
  active (running) — but note startup timestamp later than kubelet by ~12s in this repro.

3) Check CRI socket and config
- ps aux | grep containerd
- crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock images
  "FATA[0000] failed to connect: grpc: conn error: connection error: desc = "transport: authentication handshake failed: EOF""
  (indicates crictl version + runtime endpoint mismatch in this build)

4) Kubelet logs (full excerpts)
- journalctl -u kubelet -b -n 500 | sed -n '1,180p'
  key lines: 
  "I0325 14:21:02.998123 kubelet.go:203] Using cgroup driver: systemd"
  "E0325 14:21:03.001234 remote_runtime.go:201] RunPodSandbox from runtime service failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start sandbox container: error starting containerd task: ... permission denied"
  "E0325 14:21:03.002345 kubelet_pods.go:123] failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox ... plugin CNI failed: error adding container to network ... "
  "W0325 14:21:03.010000 eviction_manager.go:441] node has disk pressure"

5) dmesg and kernel messages
- dmesg | tail -n 80
  saw "overlay: too many mounts" once, and multiple "vfs: busy inodes" messages during early repro. Could be related to repeated container runtime restarts.

6) cloud-init logs (important)
- tail -n 200 /var/log/cloud-init.log
  sequence: user-data starts -> apt update -> apt install containerd (takes ~18s) -> writes /etc/containerd/config.toml -> systemctl start containerd -> then kubeadm-kubelet install script runs and starts kubelet. BUT timing shows kubelet enabled+started BEFORE containerd is active on some runs. Reproduced with precise timestamps where kubelet start precedes containerd start by ~8-18s.

7) kubeadm join output (manual run to repro)
- kubeadm join ... --v=6 | tee join.log
  error snippet: "[kubelet-check] It seems the kubelet is not running or has not yet finished starting" (expected) then later: "[preflight] WARNING: docker or containerd not found, skipping image pull"

8) CNI plugin logs (weave/flannel/amazon-vpc-cni depending on test)
- cat /var/log/cni.log (our test harness copies)
  "Error adding network: failed to find the network namespace of the process 15234: No such file or directory"
  Suggests containerd sandbox didn't create netns due to Start() failing.

9) File system and mounts
- df -h
  rootfs at 100% for ~2s in one run because /var/lib/containerd temporary dir created huge files from unpacking images while ephemeral disk not mounted yet.
- lsblk showed ephemeral EBS at /dev/nvme1n1 mounted at /mnt/data later in init; kubelet uses /var/lib/kubelet (on root) which is small default in our base image. So imagefs full heuristic plausible.

10) TLS / kubelet kubeconfig permissions
- ls -l /var/lib/kubelet/kubelet.conf -> owned by root:root, mode 0600 - kubeadm writes it after join. When kubelet starts too early there's no kubelet.conf or it has invalid certs -> kubelet loops.

Notes on things I tried and result: 
- hack: delay kubelet.service systemd unit with ExecStartPre sleep 25 -> reduces repro rate but does not eliminate (some other races).
- changed containerd unit to start earlier (WantedBy multi-user.target) -> helped in VM but not in cloud-scale repro.
- set KUBELET_CGROUP_ARGS to cgroupfs in /etc/default/kubelet -> mismatched with containerd systemd cgroup -> created different error: "Failed to start container process: cannot find cgroup in memory". Reverted.
- set net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1 via sysctl -> allowed CNI chain insertion but didn't fix pod sandbox start.
- bump ephemeral root fs size in AMI -> removed disk-pressure messages in local lab but in cloud repro still saw transient NotReady.

Intermittent traces observed only in some VM families (m6i vs c6i): m6i had slightly slower disk init and more repros. Suggests timing dependent.

Hypotheses refined: primary race is kubelet starting before container runtime is fully initialised + ephemeral disk/mounts not yet attached, creating a window where kubelet: 
- sees no runtime (connection refused) -> fails to manage pods -> triggers eviction/disk-pressure heuristics (imagefs path points to tiny root) -> node NotReady.
Secondary: misconfiguration possibility in our cloud-init template where containerd is installed but config.toml is written with incorrect runtime path when early systemctl runs.

Next steps / TODO (ordered):
1) Make a lightweight repro AMI with init script that logs timestamps to /var/log/node-boot-trace.log for events: cloud-init start, apt install containerd finished, systemctl containerd start, systemctl kubelet start, mount ephemeral device, kubeadm join start, kubelet kubeconfig created. Re-run 20 times in both m6i and c6i.
2) Add a short systemd target dependency: create file /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-dep.conf with "After=containerd.service" and "Requires=containerd.service" and test at scale. Measure repro rate.
3) Investigate mounting ephemeral disk earlier in cloud-init (write cloud-init ordering and move mount into early boot config).
4) Add preflight check in kubeadm join wrapper to wait-for-socket /run/containerd/containerd.sock with exponential backoff (crictl info check).
5) Add instrumentation to kubelet unit (Environment=KUBELET_BOOT_TS=%t) log to /var/log/kubelet-start-timestamps for later correlation.
6) If still repros, capture full strace of kubelet startup path and containerd startup to trace handshake.

Useful commands to capture when re-running repro harness: (copy/paste friendly)
- sudo journalctl -u cloud-init -o short-iso --no-pager > /tmp/journal-cloudinit.log
- sudo journalctl -u containerd -o short-iso --no-pager > /tmp/journal-containerd.log
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso --no-pager > /tmp/journal-kubelet.log
- date +%s.%N > /tmp/boot-ts-$(hostname) && echo "kubelet start: $(systemctl show -p ActiveEnterTimestamp kubelet)" >> /tmp/boot-ts-$(hostname)
- sudo ss -lpn | grep containerd || true
- sudo ls -l /run/containerd || true
- sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock status

Notes-to-self: keep the lab image minimal (no heavy apt upgrades at boot) so we isolate order-only races. If we still see repro on minimal image, then it's likely systemd unit dependency ordering, not apt timing.

References and anchors for follow-up:
- CONFLUENCE-1245: incident writeup (link above)
- Infra PR / helm chart change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452 (contains cloud-init user-data)
- Similar upstream bug: kubelet race with CRI: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/XXXXX - (note to expand)

Open questions / things to verify with AMI builders:
- Are we writing containerd config to /etc/containerd/config.toml atomically? Could partial write cause containerd to fail and restart?
- Do we set containerd to use systemd cgroups (we do) — verify runtime and kubelet cgroup driver alignment for all images.
- Can we relocate /var/lib/kubelet to ephemeral device mountpoint in image so disk-pressure heuristic points to correct mount?

If I get time before next incident: create a small helm chart that deploys a kubelet-probe DaemonSet that runs on new nodes and reports readiness of CRI socket, mount availability, and CNI health for 2 minutes after join. That will make prod debugging easier without SSHing into each node.

End of notes.
